title: Knee pain after twisting
blurb: My right knee has been sore and swollen since I twisted it.
curriculum_note: Supplementary fictional practice for the course history, physical examination and SOAP skills; not an official or predicted station.

doorway: My right knee has been sore and swollen since I twisted it.
Vital signs are available on the chart.
Perform a focused history and physical examination, discuss your plan, and document only what you obtain.
Use the time limit stated for your selected practice mode.

patient.name: Graham Wilson
patient.persona: I move stock in a grocery store, including lifting and squatting. My wife can help. We have one flight of stairs at home.
patient.opening: My right knee has been sore and swollen since I twisted it.

opening_contract.text: My right knee has been sore and swollen since I twisted it.

patient.affect: I want to know what is causing this and how to get back to my usual activities.
closing_questions: I want to know what is causing this and how to get back to my usual activities.

education_responses.student: We will protect the knee, assess stability and decide whether imaging is needed. I want to review it in one week. If it becomes hot and very swollen, you develop fever, or it locks, seek urgent assessment.
education_responses.patient: Thank you. I understand that the next steps depend on the examination and tests.

education_responses.student: We can document temporary lifting and squatting limits and discuss how you will manage stairs at home.

opening_complaint: My right knee has been sore and swollen since I twisted it.
hpi_setting: I turned while carrying a box, with my right foot planted. I did not fall.
Twisting injury on a planted foot while carrying a box; no fall.
hpi_location: Along the inside of my right knee.
hpi_radiation: No, it stays around the knee.
hpi_quality: An ache with a sharp catch if I turn.
Aching with catching pain during rotation.
hpi_severity: I can walk with a limp. The pain is 6 out of 10.
hpi_chronology: It swelled gradually that evening, not immediately.
Delayed swelling over the first evening.
hpi_timing: It catches, but I can straighten it. It has not given way.
Catching without true locking or giving way.
hpi_aggravating: Worse with twisting, stairs and deep flexion.
hpi_alleviating: Rest, ice wrapped in a towel, and elevating it.
Relief with rest, protected ice and elevation.
hpi_past_occurrence: It sometimes ached after work and felt stiff for about 5 minutes in the morning.
Prior activity-related ache and brief morning stiffness.
history_medical_history: High blood pressure and gout. I had one red, swollen big toe last year, confirmed with fluid testing.
Hypertension; crystal-confirmed gout episode last year.
history_surgery: No knee surgery. I had a hernia repaired at 30.
Hernia repair at 30; no knee surgery.
history_daily_medicines: Hydrochlorothiazide 25 milligrams daily. No regular gout medicine.
Hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily; no urate-lowering therapy.
history_smoking: I smoked half a pack daily for 10 years and quit 15 years ago.
Former smoker: 5 pack-years, quit 15 years ago.
history_alcohol: Usually three beers on Friday and three on Saturday.
history_work: I move stock in a grocery store, including lifting and squatting.
Grocery stocker; frequent lifting and squatting.
history_home: My wife can help. We have one flight of stairs at home.
Lives with wife; one flight of home stairs.
history_family_history: My mother had knee replacements for wear-and-tear arthritis.
history_other_family: My father has high blood pressure. My brother has gout.
symptom_joint_pain: The right knee hurts; no other joint hurts right now.
symptom_fatigue: I do not feel ill or unusually tired.
symptom_weakness: The ankle and foot feel normally strong.
patient_concern: I want to know what is causing this and how to get back to my usual activities.
Wants explanation and return to usual activities.

model_note.S:
CC: My right knee has been sore and swollen since I twisted it.

HPI: 54-year-old male. Right knee pain for 3 days. Twisting injury on a planted foot while carrying a box; no fall. Medial right knee pain. No radiation. Aching with catching pain during rotation. Weight bearing with limp; pain 6/10. Delayed swelling over the first evening. Catching without true locking or giving way. Worse with twisting, stairs and deep flexion. Relief with rest, protected ice and elevation. Acetaminophen 650 mg twice yesterday. Prior activity-related ache and brief morning stiffness.

PMH: Hypertension; crystal-confirmed gout episode last year.

PSH: Hernia repair at 30; no knee surgery.

Meds: Hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily; no urate-lowering therapy.

SH: Former smoker: 5 pack-years, quit 15 years ago. Approximately six beers weekly. No recreational drugs. Grocery stocker; frequent lifting and squatting. Lives with wife; one flight of home stairs.

FH: Mother: knee osteoarthritis requiring replacement. Father: hypertension; brother: gout.

Allergies: No known drug allergies.

ROS: Musculoskeletal: Right knee swelling. No other current joint pain. No generalized myalgia. General: No fever. No chills. No systemic malaise. Neurologic: No distal numbness. No paresthesias. No distal weakness.
model_note.O:
Vitals: BP 138/84 mmHg, P 78 bpm, R 16 rpm, T 98.5 F oral, Pulse Ox 98% on room air, Ht 5' 11", Wt 206 lbs

General: Alert, comfortable at rest.
Musculoskeletal: Small right knee effusion without erythema or deformity. Medial joint-line tenderness and mild warmth; no patellar or fibular-head tenderness. Right knee extends to 0 degrees and flexes to 110 degrees with pain near end flexion; mild crepitus. Knee extension 4+/5 limited by pain; ankle dorsiflexion and plantarflexion 5/5. Antalgic gait; able to take four steps.
Heart: Dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial pulses 2+ bilaterally. Regular rate and rhythm without murmur.
Lungs: Clear bilateral breath sounds.
Osteopathic: L4 right lumbar paraspinal tissue texture change and tenderness.
A: 2. Knee osteoarthritis with an acute flare
P: 1. Protect weight bearing as needed, avoid twisting/squatting and use ice, compression and elevation with safe analgesia. Assess fracture-imaging criteria and ligament stability; consider right knee MRI or orthopedics for persistent catching or true locking. Arrange modified work and review in 1 week. Fever, marked warmth, inability to bear weight or a locked knee warrants urgent reassessment.

2. If chronic symptoms persist, obtain weight-bearing radiographs when indicated and discuss strengthening/physical therapy and activity modification. Explain that degenerative changes may coexist with injury.

3. If crystal or septic arthritis remains possible with increasing warmth/effusion, arrange aspiration for crystals, cell count and culture before assuming gout. Review diuretic and gout management and safe anti-inflammatory options; explain that crystals do not exclude infection, with same-day evaluation for a hot swollen joint or fever.
